subject: ss-medical-oncology
title: Special situations in breast cancer: biology, risk assessment and tailored management

steps.tx: **Male breast cancer** is an uncommon malignancy that accounts for under 1% of all breast cancers diagnosed worldwide. The vast majority of male tumours present as estrogen receptor-positive invasive ductal carcinoma. Strong predisposing risk factors include Klinefelter syndrome, severe hepatic dysfunction, and particularly germline **BRCA2 mutations**. Systemic management follows postmenopausal female guidelines, with tamoxifen serving as the cornerstone of adjuvant and palliative endocrine therapy.

steps.tx: **Breast cancer in pregnancy** requires balanced multidisciplinary management that safeguards fetal development while providing maternal cure. When systemic therapy is needed, anthracycline-based **systemic chemotherapy** regimens can be safely administered during the second and third trimesters. In contrast, systemic cytotoxic chemotherapy during the first trimester causes excessive teratogenicity. Radiotherapy and endocrine agents are strictly contraindicated during active gestation and remain deferred until the postpartum period.

steps.tx: **Inflammatory breast cancer** is a highly lethal variant presenting with rapid breast enlargement, erythema, and marked skin edema termed **peau d'orange**. Pathological skin punch biopsy typically reveals dermal lymphatic tumour emboli. This presentation designates the tumour as clinical stage T4, specifically T4d. Standard care demands primary neoadjuvant systemic anthracycline and taxane chemotherapy, followed by modified radical mastectomy and comprehensive adjuvant chest wall radiotherapy.

steps.tx: **Phyllodes tumours** represent distinctive **fibroepithelial neoplasms** composed of monoclonal stromal proliferation and benign epithelial elements. Histological criteria divide them into benign, borderline, and malignant grades based on stromal cellularity, cellular atypia, stromal overgrowth, and mitotic rate. Wide local surgical excision with clear negative histological margins of at least one centimetre represents primary treatment. Lymph node dissection is rarely required because malignant spread occurs haematogenously.

Wide local surgical excision with clear margins provides primary treatment. Lymph node dissection is rarely required.

steps.tx: Preinvasive **ductal carcinoma in situ** is commonly managed with breast-conserving surgery followed by adjuvant whole-breast radiotherapy to optimise local control. In hormone receptor-positive disease, adjuvant endocrine therapy with 5 years of daily oral **tamoxifen** significantly reduces the subsequent risk of both ipsilateral and contralateral invasive breast cancer events. For postmenopausal patients, an aromatase inhibitor provides an effective alternative to tamoxifen depending on vascular and bone health.

For postmenopausal patients, an aromatase inhibitor provides an effective alternative.

steps.tx: **Paget disease** of the nipple presents clinically as a chronic, eczematoid erythematous nipple-areolar eruption with surface scaling or crusting. Microscopic inspection demonstrates infiltration of the nipple epidermis by malignant **intraepidermal Paget cells** displaying large pale cytoplasm and prominent nucleoli. The vast majority of cases harbor an underlying ductal carcinoma in situ or invasive ductal adenocarcinoma, necessitating thorough bilateral diagnostic mammography and breast magnetic resonance imaging.

right.title: Benign Nipple Eczema
points: Bilateral and responsive to topical steroids

steps.tx: The section shows large pale **Paget cells** scattered through the **nipple surface layer**, each with abundant clear cytoplasm and a prominent central nucleus. These cells signal an eczema like nipple rash that never heals with creams. Almost every case hides an **underlying cancer focus** such as DCIS nearby, shown inset, so persistent one sided nipple change demands **full breast imaging** of both breast tissue and nodes.
steps.say: Paget disease shows large pale malignant cells wandering within the nipple surface layer, visible here among normal skin cells, with an inset of coexisting ductal cancer in situ. Clinically this looks like a persistent one sided eczema like nipple rash with scaling or crusting. Because most cases conceal nearby ductal cancer in situ or invasive cancer, lasting nipple change needs complete breast imaging rather than steroid cream alone.

steps.tx: Optimal management of older adults requires objective **geriatric assessment** rather than chronological age alone. Validated instruments such as the **CARG toxicity** risk calculator accurately predict severe grade 3 to 5 chemotherapy toxicities. Evaluating functional status, cognitive reserve, comorbidities, and polypharmacy helps clinicians tailor treatment intensity, deciding between full-dose cytotoxic regimens, dose modifications, single-agent options, or primary endocrine therapy.

steps.tx: **Oligometastatic breast cancer** describes an intermediate biological state with limited metastatic spread, typically five or fewer detectable distant lesions. In carefully selected patients with controlled primary disease, delivering definitive local ablative therapies such as **stereotactic radiotherapy** or surgical metastasectomy alongside systemic therapy can prolong disease-free survival. Multidisciplinary tumor board review ensures aggressive local consolidation is applied only when widespread micrometastatic progression remains unlikely.
